highlights.title: 编队的拓扑与角色一起优化：把组合问题写成谱函数
highlights.title_en: Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems
highlights.glance: 把图结构、信道状态与角色分配编成三个张量做一次收缩，耦合度量恰好等于非平凡拉普拉斯特征值的均值——最优领导者从张量代数里自己长出来，不需要任何启发式规则

essay.v: 编队控制里有个绕不开的组合爆炸：谁跟谁连（拓扑）和谁当头（角色）是耦合在一起的。先定拓扑再挑 leader，会丢掉大部分可行解；两个一起搜，又是阶乘级的规模。北航这支团队给的办法不是把搜索加速，而是换掉搜索本身——把两个离散选择变成可求导的对象。
三个张量，一次收缩
框架用三个张量分别编码三件事：图的邻接结构、随时间变化的信道状态、以及角色分配。三者的收缩给出一个耦合度量，而这个度量恰好等于该图上非平凡拉普拉斯特征值的均值。这一点是整篇文章的支点：一个原本要枚举组合才能评估的量，被改写成了可以直接求梯度的谱函数。
于是联合优化就落到了连续目标上。作者的做法是把谱梯度流限制在一个 Tucker 压缩的子空间里，配合增量更新，并从上一次的解热启动。在温和假设下，Tucker 压缩保证多项式复杂度，梯度流的收敛性也被证明了。仿真显示，随着智能体数量增长，它的扩展性显著优于穷举组合搜索。
领导者不是被指定的，是算出来的
最耐读的一点是领导者的产生方式。传统做法要么靠启发式规则（度数最高、离目标最近、编号最小），要么由外部直接指定；在这篇里，最优 leader 直接从张量代数的结果里涌现。换句话说，角色不再是一个需要另设一套算法去挑的离散变量，而是同一个优化问题的副产品——这正是「联合」二字的实际含义。
代价也要说清楚：这是合作式编队控制的设定，全篇没有对手、没有信息不对称下的策略性欺骗，读它不要指望看到博弈结构。它的价值在别处——它示范了怎么把一个组合设计问题降级成连续优化问题。
怎么读这篇

来源与可核性：Nature Communications，2026 年 10 月 21 日上线，开放获取，作者来自北京航空航天大学自动化科学与电气工程学院及杭州创新研究院等，收稿 2026-04-15、录用 2026-09-30，约五个半月的审稿周期，ORCID、基金号与利益冲突声明齐全。本次抓取到的内容以摘要与页面元数据为准，正文图表未能取得；文中关于扩展性的表述来自摘要的定性结论（随智能体数量增长显著优于穷举组合搜索），没有具体曲线数值，引用时宜按定性处理。
局限：全部结果在仿真中验证；Tucker 压缩所依赖的「温和假设」与梯度流收敛证明的具体条件要看正文才知道边界在哪里；也没有与学习型方法（例如多智能体强化学习）做数值对照——它走的是解析优化路线，不是学习路线。把它当性能标杆引用是不合适的，可复用的是建模思路。
「把离散的组合选择变成可微的谱函数」——这是整篇最值得整段抄走的动作。
迁移价值有两条。建模层：遇到「结构加分工」这类耦合的组合设计问题，先问目标能不能写成谱函数——特征值均值、代数连通度、有效电阻都是候选，写成了就从组合优化降级成连续优化。工程层：热启动配增量更新这套写法是给在线重配置准备的，编队中途加人、减人、链路变差时不必从头解一遍。

highlights.title: 雷达与干扰机的非均衡博弈：在线自博弈学互动，离线扩散修分布
highlights.title_en: Diffusion-enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive interference control in bilateral cognitive radar games
highlights.summary: In complex electromagnetic environments, adaptive signal-emitting systems operate under partial observability, asymmetric information, and dynamically evolving spectrum interactions, posing significant challenges to interference-aware decision-making. To address these challenges, this paper formulates the signal interaction process as a partially observable stochastic game and proposes a Bilateral Intelligent Game Policy Optimization Architecture (BIGPOA). Within this framework, a two-stage Diffusion-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (Diff-MAPPO) algorithm is developed. In the online stage, Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) with self-play training is employed to learn interactive behaviors between sensing and interference agents. In the offline stage, a diffusion model refines the learned policies through trajectory-level distribution regularization, while Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN)-guided optimization promotes high-value decision generation. Experimental results demonstrate that Diff-MAPPO achieves faster convergence, higher interference effectiveness, and improved energy efficiency compared with representative reinforcement learning baselines, while maintaining robust performance under dynamic and uncertain signal environments.
highlights.summary_short: In complex electromagnetic environments, adaptive signal-emitting systems operate under partial observability, asymmetric information, and dynamically evolving spectrum interactions, posing significant challenges to interference-aware decision-making.
highlights.glance: 明说这不是均衡问题：在线用自博弈 MAPPO 让双方共同演化，离线用扩散模型对轨迹分布做正则——扩散模型在这里是策略平滑器，不是世界模型

essay.v: 电磁对抗里最常见的失败模式不是策略不够聪明，而是策略不稳定：对手一直在变，奖励信号跟着漂，MAPPO 训出来的策略在震荡里来回摆。把 MAPPO 直接搬进雷达—干扰机这类场景，两个具体问题会同时冒出来——部分可观测让你推断不出对手行为，非平稳的奖励动态让策略震荡、收敛不稳。这篇给的解法很特别：它不追求均衡解，干脆承认这是非均衡问题，然后把「学互动」和「稳策略」拆成两个阶段。
先承认它不是均衡问题

作者把自适应感知系统与智能干扰源之间的信号交互建模为部分可观测随机博弈，并命名为「双边智能博弈」：双方信息不对称、都只看得到部分观测、训练期间都拿不到对手策略，两边的策略通过对抗持续共同演化。以雷达与干扰的交互为代表性例子，双方都被当作具有不对称信息的智能决策者。作者的取舍说得很直白——这套框架强调非均衡条件下的策略共同演化，而不是静态均衡解。这个表态值得单独记一笔：很多真实对抗场景里，均衡本来就不存在，或者算不出来。
相应的架构叫 BIGPOA，建模粒度落在信号参数级，而不是抽象的战术级：双方调的是什么信号参数、这些参数如何互相压制，都被写进了博弈的形式化里。框架还显式地把能量效率纳入优化目标。
在线学互动，离线修分布
第一阶段是在线的：用 MAPPO 配自博弈训练，学习感知方与干扰方之间的交互行为。第二阶段是离线的：用扩散模型对学到的策略做轨迹级分布正则，也就是把在线阶段学到的轨迹分布再做一次提纯与平滑；同时用 DDQN 引导的优化去推动高价值决策的生成。分工很清楚——在线负责探索与适应，离线负责稳定与样本效率。
论文列的四条贡献与此一一对应：非均衡的感知—干扰博弈框架、信号参数级的双边智能优化架构、扩散增强的多智能体学习算法（Diff-MAPPO）、以及在高度动态的雷达测试床上的验证。作者还单独做了计算复杂度分析来说明可扩展性。
怎么读这篇
来源与可核性：爱思唯尔旗下 Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence，DOI 10.1016/j.engappai.2026.116525，雷达记录的可用日期为 2026-10-20。出版方页面上可核实摘要、四条亮点、关键词、引言与结论，以及作者贡献声明与利益冲突声明（无已知竞争性财务利益）。

局限要说在前：本次只取到摘要、亮点与分节文本，收敛速度、干扰效能与能量效率的具体数值、基线清单、随机种子设置都没能取得，因此这里的判断只覆盖方法结构，不覆盖数字。实验全部在一个仿真化的雷达—干扰机交互场景里完成，没有硬件在环或实测数据。文章自己把「异质感知智能与部分可观测」列为最能体现优势的条件，反过来讲，在对称性更强、观测更完整的场景里优势可能收窄。把它的绝对数值当基准引用是不合适的，可复用的是两阶段这个拆分。
「强调动态适应而非静态均衡解」——这句话是这类对抗问题最该先想清楚的前提。
可迁移的启发是两阶段结构本身。凡是对抗训练出现策略震荡、样本效率塌方的场合，都可以试一试「在线自博弈学行为、离线生成模型做分布正则」。更具体一点：扩散模型在这里不是用来生成训练数据的，而是当成策略分布的平滑器在用——这个用法比把它当世界模型更省，也更容易接进已有的 MAPPO 流水线。如果你的对抗环境里对手也在学，先别急着找均衡，想想能不能把「适应」和「稳定」拆成两个目标分别优化。

highlights.title: 卡特尔真的在执行吗：用反事实市场审计 LLM 定价智能体
highlights.title_en: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
highlights.summary: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. A war forced into training is learned, but mostly only where it was forced. Against their own copies, deterred and matching agents can earn the same cartel profits, but only matching ones can enforce them, and then thinly: as a by-product and only against large cuts. Q-learners enforce collusion only in pricing. Prompted LLMs reach cartel-like outcomes mostly through rules that ignore the market. Outcome measures cannot tell these cases apart; the audit can.
highlights.summary_short: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished.
highlights.section: LLM 多智能体与社会模拟
highlights.glance: 高价格不等于卡特尔：作者克隆整个市场、强迫一名成员偏离一期，看对手是否惩罚——结果指标分不清的情形，这套审计能分清

essay.v: 一批评测报告说 LLM 定价智能体会把价格抬到竞争水平之上，于是「LLM 会合谋」成了 headlines。但这篇论文指出一个被跳过的前提：卡特尔之所以是卡特尔，不在于大家都卖高价，而在于有人作弊时会被惩罚。没有执行机制的高价，只是各自碰巧采用的定价规则而已。作者给出的，是一套能把这两者区分开的审计。
把偏离实验做成配对检验

审计的核心操作是克隆。从某个保存下来的市场状态出发，复制整个市场与所有智能体——每个智能体的历史与笔记、以及接下来所有的随机抽取都一并复制；在克隆体里强迫一名成员偏离一期（定价场景是降价百分之十，交易场景是打出单期最优反应），然后两个副本继续跑下去。因为模型调用带有按会话、智能体、期设定的采样种子，两个副本在偏离改变它们所见之前会给出完全相同的回答。作者把这一步的渊源说得很清楚：这等于把 Calvano 等人 2020 年那套 Q 学习偏离实验，改造成对随机 LLM 智能体可用的配对比较，也就是共同随机数。
可复现性的诚实程度值得单独表扬：在没有偏离的 A/A 检验里，走 vLLM 服务的副本有百分之九十四到九十八的调用给出一致答案，走 OpenAI 接口的只有百分之二十三到四十五（因为那里的种子是 best-effort）。作者明确写了这会带来噪声但不会带来偏差——这种把工具链缺陷摆到台面上的写法，比只报漂亮数字可信得多。
学的是对手奖励什么，但只学它会去试的
结论分几层。用 GRPO 训练的小模型（Qwen3-0.6B）学到的东西，受限于它们本来会去尝试什么。自博弈下它们学成固定规则、完全无视对手；对上一个以牙还牙、复制它上期价格的对手，学成被威慑——价格高、不回应、偏离有利可图；对上一个作弊的对手，学成跟随降价，却从不学那个能真正威慑对方的高代价价格战，因为它们几乎不会去试。把价格战强行塞进训练是能学会的，但基本只在被强塞的那些状态里学会。
最关键的一条：把训练后的智能体和自己的副本配对，被威慑型与跟随型能赚到同样的卡特尔利润，但只有跟随型（学到了以牙还牙）能真正执行它，而且执行得很薄——它是副产品，且只对大幅降价有效：百分之十的降价在九个种子里只有四个让偏离者吃亏，换成约百分之十六的最优反应降价才升到七个。
对照表里的另外几条

表格 Q 学习者在定价博弈里的对手反应是 1.30 加减 0.11，显著高于不惩罚的基线，是可靠的惩罚者；但在交易场景里是 0.00 加减 0.00，完全不惩罚——合谋的执行只出现在定价，不出现在交易。未经训练的 LLM 达到类卡特尔结果，主要靠的是无视市场的固定规则：Qwen3-8B 的定价指数随货币单位从 13.12 变到 5.08，这是锚定而不是策略。GPT-5.2 在 Fish 等人协议下的两次类卡特尔会话经重新检验，对手反应 1.01 加减 0.11，确实在惩罚——但那两次会话是事后从八次里挑出来的，这一条要打折扣看。
怎么读这篇

来源：arXiv 2610.28787，马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校与洛厄尔分校，45 页正文、13 幅图、20 张表，是预印本、未经同行评议。数字全部取自正文表格，可信度高，但样本规模要看清：GRPO 定价结果以种子 0 为主并标注了种子一致性（如九分之四），交易场景的智能体数量在一到五之间、市场深度在 0.25 到 4 之间扫描。作者自己列了四类安慰剂（单独交易者、只算当期的短视目标、训练时把折扣因子设为零、同一提示有对手与无对手）与两类正对照（被指示使用触发策略的模型、定价博弈里的 Q 学习者）。
另一个边界要摆明：审计能证伪但不能穷尽证明。它只能说「在这些偏离下，对手的反应显著高于不惩罚的基线」，无法排除存在别的偏离路径。作者也明说这套审计是给评测用的，不是给监管定案用的，并单列了一节讨论双重用途。此外，审计在交易场景里判出的 pruning bias（删单偏差）提示了另一种伪装：看似有反应，其实是订单被剪掉造成的假象。
「结果指标分不清这些情形，审计能。」这是全文最锋利的一句。
可迁移的启发有三条。第一，评估多智能体的经济行为时不要只看结果指标，要做反事实偏离检验——而且一定要配共同随机数，否则 LLM 的采样噪声会淹没信号。第二，「学会什么」被「会去尝试什么」死死限制住：强化学习只能在策略已经探索到的区域里放大，想让智能体学到某种行为，先确认它在探索中真的出现过。第三，也是最有政策含义的一条：高价格与可执行的高价格是两件事，反垄断真正该盯的是后者。

highlights.title: 广告主少或展示位少时，GSP 自动竞价均衡可以精确算出来
highlights.title_en: GSP Autobidding Equilibria with Few Advertisers or Slots
highlights.summary: In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ranking. We prove that exact autobidding equilibria under budget and return-on-investment (ROI) constraints can be computed in polynomial time whenever either the number $n$ of advertisers or the number $K$ of display slots is fixed. Our algorithms rely on two structural reductions. With few advertisers, the payment polytopes of tied bid layers combine by a Minkowski sum, giving a fixed-dimensional representation of exponentially many rankings. With few slots, budget equilibria admit threshold recovery and an exact submodular description of attainable payments at the display boundary. For ROI, we prove that every group-consecutive equilibrium has a representative with at most $K+2$ nonunit multipliers, preserving the item and price in every displayed slot. In each case, the reduction leads to polynomially many systems of polynomial equations and inequalities in bounded dimension. The algorithms compute exact multipliers and explicit distributions over valid group-consecutive rankings, with support at most $n+1$; for ROI with few slots, this improves to $\min\{n+1,K+3\}$.
highlights.summary_short: In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ran…
highlights.glance: 赞助购物拍卖的精确均衡计算被证明在固定广告主数 n 或固定展示位 K 时是多项式时间的——指数级的一族排序被两条结构性归约压成了多项式级的一族代表结果

essay.v: 赞助购物拍卖有个反直觉的结构：一个从来没有被展示的商品，可能决定了好几个展示位的价格。在广义第二价格且排除自我定价的规则下，展示中的商品支付的是「另一个广告主」的最高次位出价，而这个出价可能远远落在最后一个展示位之外。于是分配与支付被同一条全局排序绑死——这正是均衡算不出来的根源。既有结果已经把精确计算放进 FIXP、把近似计算证明成 PPAD-难，这篇问的是另一个问题：如果市场在结构上很小呢？
原则一：逐层凸化

固定广告主数 n 时，每个并列出价层里至多包含 n 个价值组。不同层之间的顺序组合起来是指数级的完整排序，但每一层贡献的支付矩阵只由它自己的顺序决定。于是所有可达的总支付矩阵构成一族局部多胞体的闵可夫斯基和；在固定维度下可以枚举它的顶点，并为每个顶点配上一个合法排序。预算情形下压缩期望支付向量，投资回报率情形下则把价值也放进局部表示并压缩期望剩余。指数级的一族排序就此塌缩成多项式级的一族代表结果。
原则二：展示边界
固定展示位 K 时会撞上另一个麻烦：阈值处可能有任意多个广告主并列，排序的选择数与支付的坐标数都不再有界。作者的做法是抓住展示与未展示的边界。对预算情形，第 K 高的出价能恢复出除至多 K 减一个阈值以上广告主之外的全部乘子；任意大的阈值并列所对应的可达支付，被刻画成一个子模基多胞体，再把这个多胞体与剩余的预算区间求交，从而消掉它的支付坐标。
对投资回报率情形则给出另一个结构性结果：任意组连续均衡都可以变换成一个至多只有 K 加 2 个非单位乘子的均衡，并且保持每个展示位上的商品与价格完全不变——两个阈值以下的定价见证，或者一个通用阈值见证，就足以保住相关的尾部信息。这种稀疏性把乘子搜索压到了有界维度。
复杂度账本

四条结果的时间复杂度与均衡分布的支撑大小分别是：固定 n 的预算与投资回报率情形都是 M 的 n 立方加 n 平方量级次方、支撑 n 加 1；固定 K 的预算情形是 M 的 K 立方量级次方、支撑 n 加 1；固定 K 的投资回报率情形是 M 的 K 平方量级次方、支撑 n 加 1 与 K 加 3 中的较小者。每个归约最终都归结为多项式多个、变量数有界、次数至多为二的系统，剩下的交给标准的精确多项式可行性判定。要注意「多项式」在这里的确切含义：指数长在 n 或 K 上，多项式是对商品总数 M 而言。
怎么读这篇

来源：arXiv 2610.29310，预印本、未经同行评议，领域为计算机科学与博弈论。它引用的前置结果是一条可靠的坐标系：Dütting 等人给出了赞助购物模型下投资回报率均衡的存在性与为二的无政府价格紧界；Hansen、Li、Nie 证明了预算均衡与投资回报率均衡的存在性、多项式大小的均衡支撑、精确计算的 FIXP 成员资格，以及近似计算的 PPAD-难。这篇是在这条线上的结构性刻画，全篇不含实验。
局限：结果属于「固定参数可解」这一类，n 或 K 一大就失效，而真实的广告市场里这两个数往往都不小；论文给出的是精确的代数乘子与显式的排序分布，数值实现与工程可用性没有讨论。另外它针对的是「无自我定价」的广义第二价格规则，规则一变，支付耦合的结构就跟着变了。
「一个从未被展示的商品，可能决定好几个赢家的价格」——这句是理解整篇文章难度的钥匙。
迁移价值在方法论。面对「组合爆炸来自排序、而排序又决定支付」这类问题，先问哪一层的局部结构允许凸化（闵可夫斯基和、子模基多胞体），再问边界上哪些坐标可以被消掉；这两步做完，剩下的常常就是一个低维可行性问题。做拍卖或匹配市场的人可以直接把「固定参数是否可解」当成一条默认追问：全量 PPAD-难不等于所有规模都难，把 n 或 K 固定下来往往能换出一整套精确算法。

highlights.title_en: The Butterfly Effect in LLM Social Simulations: From Architecture Sensitivity to Robustness Audits
highlights.summary: A butterfly effect occurs when a local perturbation propagates through a system and produces divergence in its collective outcome. In LLM social simulations, this creates a particular challenge for scientific inference: sensitivity to implementation choices can enter agent interactions and alter the collective outcomes on which scientific claims are based. We study this problem through a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma and a social-media echo chamber, spanning representation- and design-level perturbations across four LLM families. We find that controlled perturbations can substantially alter collective outcomes, with sensitivity varying across both perturbations and models. In the Prisoner's Dilemma, changing only the representation of a matched persona shifts two-agent cooperation by 75.2 percentage points for GPT-5.2, while game framing and memory representation produce smaller or less consistent effects. Multi-agent interaction further reshapes representation sensitivity, producing amplification or attenuation depending on the model and perturbation. In the echo-chamber simulation, persona representation changes interaction targeting and is accompanied by divergence in collective interaction structure, extending representation sensitivity from agent behavior to network-level outcomes. These results show that robustness cannot be inferred from a single simulation configuration and that local sensitivity can change as it propagates through interaction. We introduce TRAILS (Taxonomy for Robustness Audits In LLM Simulations) and the Social Simulation Audit Card as a framework for systematically auditing these dependencies and calibrating the scope of scientific claims to the robustness evidence that supports them.

highlights.section: LLM 多智能体与社会模拟
highlights.glance: 只把人设从 Plain 改成 Descriptive，十轮囚徒困境的合作率就从百分之九十八点二掉到百分之二十三；而多智能体交互会把这种局部敏感放大或衰减，方向取决于模型

essay.v: 用大语言模型做社会模拟的人越来越多，结论也下得越来越敢：不只是「可能发生什么」，而是「为什么发生、什么时候发生、下一步该怎么办」。这篇论文给这个趋势踩了一脚刹车。它只改动了同一个人设的书写方式，其余全部保持不变，十轮重复囚徒困境里的合作率就从百分之九十八点二掉到百分之二十三。七十五点二个百分点的落差不是换模型、换博弈、换参数造成的，只是把人设从 Plain 写成了 Descriptive。
敏感性的来源不是世界观，是写法

作者在两类受控模拟范式上做实验：重复囚徒困境（区分固定对手与互惠式的模型对模型交互）与社交媒体回声室，覆盖四个模型族，扰动横跨表示层与设计层。第一层结果是：人设格式在四个模型族上都产生了显著的合作率变化，但幅度差得离谱——维度内最大对比从 deepseek 的七点七个百分点，到 claude-haiku-4-5 的七十七点七个百分点。博弈框架只在一部分模型上显著，记忆表示则只有 gpt-5.2 出现了显著的最大合作率差异，六点二个百分点。也就是说，敏感性既随扰动变，也随模型变，无法从单一配置外推。
第二层更值得注意：多智能体交互会重塑这种敏感性。互惠式的模型对模型交互，在三个模型族上放大了同一个人设扰动，在第四个上却衰减了它。局部差异传到集体层面时不是简单累加——它可能被放大，也可能被吃掉。
从个体行为一路传到网络结构

回声室模拟把这条链路接到了网络级结果上：一百个智能体、十五轮、立场固定。以 gpt-5.2 为例，动作一致率高达百分之九十九点七，但选择交互对象的一致率只有百分之五十五点一——动作看起来没变，跟谁说话全变了。Prose 写法使跨群组指向增加五点一五个百分点（百分之九十五置信区间四点二二到六点零七），到第 15 轮累积的立场同配性低了零点一九四。人设表示就这样从个体行为一路传到了集体的交互结构上面。
怎么读这篇
来源：arXiv 2610.28981，南加州大学，Emilio Ferrara 组，代码与数据在 GitHub 公开，是预印本、未经同行评议。统计口径交代得比较规范：三十个配对种子、百分之九十五置信区间、Holm 校正的配对 Wilcoxon 检验。四个模型族为 GPT-5.2、Claude Haiku 4.5、Gemini 2.5 Flash、DeepSeek V4 Flash。
局限要摆明：这是单一实验室、单一代码库下的结果。扰动清单虽然系统——作者把扰动分成表示层与设计层两张表，覆盖格式、分隔符、输出模式、指令顺序、角色与消息位置、命名措辞、记忆表示、上下文窗口、消息元数据、交互协议、干预设计、环境结构、种群与规模等——但不可能穷尽所有实现选择，模型族也只测了四家。另外，显著的敏感性说明的是「结论依赖于实现」，不等于「结论错了」；它给出的是证据强度的上界，不是证伪。
「鲁棒性无法从单一模拟配置推断出来」——这句话应该印在每一篇大语言模型社会模拟论文的方法章节前面。

可迁移的启发是：把它提出的分层扰动清单当检查表用。它把扰动分成表示层与设计层，并按微观（模型基底、智能体设定、内部状态与时间性）、中观（交互协议、干预设计）、宏观（环境结构、种群与规模）分层。做模拟的人可以按这张表逐项跑敏感性扫描，再按作者给的社会模拟审计卡把「结论的适用范围」明写出来：哪些扰动下结论站得住（与目标情境相关的扰动只应当限定结论的表述），哪些扰动下结论塌了（与目标情境无关的扰动一旦显著，就是实现敏感的铁证）。

trends: 今天这批条目有一个共同的方法论转向：从「把结果算出来」转向「问这个结果站不站得住」。三篇各自给出了一种证伪工具——卡特尔审计用反事实克隆市场检验高价是否真的被执行，社会模拟用分层扰动清单检验结论是否只属于某一种实现，拍卖理论则用固定参数归约说明「全量难」不等于「所有规模都难」。
「看起来一样」与「真的一样」之间的裂缝正在被系统性量化。定价智能体的高价格可能是锚定规则，也可能是可执行的卡特尔，结果指标分不清而审计能分清；同一个人设的两种写法下动作一致率高达百分之九十九点七，却掩盖了交互对象一致率只有百分之五十五点一。共同结论是：只看聚合指标会系统性地误判机制。
结构上的「小」正在被当作可解性资源，而不是无奈的退让。赞助购物拍卖在广告主数或展示位固定时，精确均衡能对商品总数多项式时间算出；两条归约——逐层凸化的闵可夫斯基和、展示边界上的子模基多胞体——都是把指数级的排序族压成多项式级的代表结果。这与「一旦 PPAD-难就放弃」的默认反应形成了直接对照。
对抗场景正在主动放弃均衡假设。雷达与干扰机的交互被明确写成非均衡的部分可观测随机博弈，双方在训练中都拿不到对手策略、策略持续共同演化，优化目标从「求均衡」换成「求自适应」；配套的是在线自博弈学互动、离线扩散模型做轨迹分布正则的两阶段拆分，用生成模型当策略平滑器而非世界模型。
组合式的多智能体设计问题在换掉搜索本身。编队的拓扑与角色是一对联立的离散选择，穷举是阶乘级；把图结构、信道状态、角色分配编成三个张量并做一次收缩，耦合度量恰好等于非平凡拉普拉斯特征值的均值，最优领导者从代数里涌现而不是由启发式指定。同一天的另一面是理论端走到了固定参数可解——从最抽象的复杂度刻画到最具体的谱优化目标，今天这批条目把这条光谱的两端都占上了。

radar.title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
radar.summary: Abstract Knowledge-constrained network inference enables the reconstruction of regulatory programmes from high-dimensional biological data, yet the conditions under which shared and context-specific structures can be reliably identified remain poorly understood. Pablo Rodriguez-Mier et al. recently introduced CORNETO, a framework for multi-sample constrained inference. Here we reproduce, evaluate and extend CORNETO in terms of robustness, identifiability and bias–variance trade-offs. Using dynamic haematopoiesis and stable cortical datasets, we systematically assess four network reconstruction paradigms while preserving the original method-specific evaluation procedures and benchmark definitions. We show that multi-sample inference generally improves robustness and reproducibility, although gains in predictive performance depend on biological context and the completeness of the prior network. To enhance stability, we introduce bootstrap aggregation and selective re-expansion strategies that improve consensus robustness and recovery while preserving context-specific signals without modifying the underlying optimization scheme or sacrificing generality. Across datasets and methods, our results reveal distinct inference regimes governed by sample availability, prior knowledge and regularization. Together, these findings position network reconstruction as a regime-dependent learning problem and provide practical principles for robust multi-sample biological network inference.

Pablo Rodriguez-Mier et al.

radar.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
radar.summary: Abstract The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

radar.title: Multiagent Assortment Optimization in Sequential Matching Markets
radar.summary: Motivated by the challenges faced by choice-based matching platforms, in this work, we study a generalization of the two-sided assortment optimization model. Specifically, this model consists of two sides (e.g., customers and suppliers) who have preferences over the opposite side in the form of discrete choice models. A matching is realized through a two-step process where the platform’s decision is to initially present to each agent on one side an assortment of users of the opposite side. The ultimate goal of the platform is to maximize the total expected revenue collected from the matching. Because of the computational complexity of this problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms with constant-factor guarantees for the constrained version of the problem under general choice preferences. First, to the best of our knowledge, we are the first to draw connections with the literature of submodular optimization and show that one-sided choice-oblivious approaches perform arbitrarily badly. Second, we show that, for the general setting, there exists a two-sided choice-aware randomized algorithm that achieves a [Formula: see text]-approximation factor, which is the best possible. Third, we design an algorithm that is asymptotically optimal when one side follows the well-known multinomial logit (MNL) choice model under the small probability regime. Fourth, we provide a simple and effective algorithm with a [Formula: see text]-approximation guarantee for the unconstrained setting, with both sides following MNL models. Finally, we assess the performance of our proposed methods with a detailed computational study and discuss several extensions. Funding: M. radar.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
radar.summary: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, over 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell-type-specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

radar.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
radar.summary: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

Simple and Effective: A Deterministic Auction with Support Information
radar.summary: We study an auction design problem where a seller aims to sell a single item to multiple bidders with independent private values. The seller knows only an upper bound on these values and does not know their distribution. The objective is to devise a deterministic auction mechanism effective across a broad set of distributions. radar.title: Diffusion-enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive interference control in bilateral cognitive radar games
radar.summary: In complex electromagnetic environments, adaptive signal-emitting systems operate under partial observability, asymmetric information, and dynamically evolving spectrum interactions, posing significant challenges to interference-aware decision-making. To address these challenges, this paper formulates the signal interaction process as a partially observable stochastic game and proposes a Bilateral Intelligent Game Policy Optimization Architecture (BIGPOA). Within this framework, a two-stage Diffusion-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (Diff-MAPPO) algorithm is developed. In the online stage, Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) with self-play training is employed to learn interactive behaviors between sensing and interference agents. In the offline stage, a diffusion model refines the learned policies through trajectory-level distribution regularization, while Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN)-guided optimization promotes high-value decision generation. Experimental results demonstrate that Diff-MAPPO achieves faster convergence, higher interference effectiveness, and improved energy efficiency compared with representative reinforcement learning baselines, while maintaining robust performance under dynamic and uncertain signal environments.

radar.summary: This study proposes a cooperative capture system in which two allied unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) jointly deploy a capture net to intercept noncooperative vessels in naval environments. To overcome the limitations of traditional rule-based methods subjected to environmental uncertainties, a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework is developed within a high-fidelity, unity-based simulation environment incorporating the Gerstner wave and wind disturbance models. Each agent utilizes an egocentric polar coordinate observation space; distance values are normalized via a nonlinear rational function to prioritize close-range sensitivity, while angular discontinuities are resolved through trigonometric transformations. The Multi-Agent POsthumous Credit Assignment algorithm is adopted within a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution architecture, enabling robust strategy learning through posthumous credit assignment even when agents exit the environment. The reward structure is designed hierarchically, combining sparse event rewards for capture success with dense continuous rewards based on formation maintenance, target approach, and heading alignment. Quantitative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MARL-based approach significantly outperforms the modified Line-of-Sight guidance law, achieving a 65% capture success rate and a three-fold reduction in formation collapse under dynamic sea conditions. This study confirms that the proposed framework effectively enables autonomous USVs to learn complex, coordinated maneuvers for physical maritime interdiction, providing a robust solution for securing maritime security.

radar.title: Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange
radar.summary: Unlocking Value Through Nonprofit Resource Sharing Nonprofit organizations often operate under tight budgets while idle equipment, unused space, and shareable skills and expertise are frequently underutilized, with existing resource exchanges in the nonprofit sector limited to bilateral barter or relatively homogeneous resources. In “Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange,” Huang et al. propose Sharing With a Purpose (SWAP), a resource-sharing system that enables nonprofits to exchange heterogeneous resources without monetary payments. SWAP combines an auction-based process, SWAPcredit valuation, and integer optimization to facilitate multilateral exchanges, allowing nonprofits to obtain needed resources by contributing resources of their own. The authors implement this market design through the SWAP Hub, a digital platform deployed with nonprofit communities in multiple regions. Through repeated exchange episodes, participating organizations have shared not only physical assets but also a wide range of skills, services, and expertise, including marketing, management, event planning, and organizational development. The study demonstrates how innovative market design can unlock latent value in community resources, alleviate resource constraints, and encourage new connections and collaboration among nonprofit organizations.

radar.title: A Survey of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from the Perspective of Task Characteristics
radar.summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the relationship between agents' rewards determines part of the learning problem. Shared rewards give rise to credit assignment and coordinated action selection; opposed rewards require responses to an adapting opponent. Both relationships occur in mixed tasks. This survey takes these task differences as the starting point for reviewing MARL, complementing classifications based on algorithms, training frameworks, or application domains. The analysis follows task characteristics, interaction types, and algorithmic mechanisms across cooperative, competitive, and mixed cooperative-competitive settings. It covers the basic formulations and training and execution paradigms, then compares representative methods in terms of their mechanisms, applicability, and limitations. Path planning, task allocation, pursuit-evasion and adversarial engagement, autonomous driving, and resource allocation illustrate how information access and operational constraints affect method selection. The concluding discussion concerns non-stationarity, scaling, safety, and the evidence needed for deployment. The comparisons support method selection under stated task conditions, without treating applicability as independent of the task being addressed.

radar.title: Emergent collaborative scheduling in satellite swarms: A distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning approach with adaptive experience evolution
radar.summary: Autonomous collaboration among multiple Earth observation satellites is essential for improving the performance of satellite swarms. However, this task is challenging because of limited onboard computing resources and unstable inter-satellite links, particularly when global coordination is required under communication constraints. Traditional centralized optimization methods often adapt poorly to dynamic observation requests, whereas existing multi-agent approaches may incur communication overhead that hinders practical deployment. To address this issue, we propose a distributed scheduling framework that enables emergent global coordination through local agent interactions and formulates the problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP). Specifically, we develop L-QTRAN, a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that enables satellites to coordinate based on local observations with limited communication. To alleviate the non-stationarity inherent in dynamic swarm environments, we introduce an Adaptive Experience Evolution (AEE) mechanism. This mechanism follows the survival-of-the-fittest principle by selectively retaining elite transition experiences, thereby accelerating the development of cooperative strategies. Furthermore, a Random Segment Sampling (RSS) technique is introduced to improve training stability and convergence in high-dimensional solution spaces. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline methods under weak-communication conditions and achieves sub-second response times, highlighting its potential for autonomous satellite swarms operating in dynamic environments.

A Deep Learning Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
radar.summary: In the world of large language models (LLMs), prompt injection attacks are a severe security risk that can circumvent the instructions given to AI agents and potentially cause damage. In agentic architectures, the vulnerabilities are magnified because of the increased attack surfaces which are present in the use of tools, APIs and chains of reasoning. The vulnerabilities are compounded in agentic architectures as the tools used, APIs called, and chains of reasoning become a larger attack surface, resulting in an increased sense of unreliability. Paraphrased, adaptive, and context-aware attacks are not thwarted by rule-based and static prompt engineering defenses. This paper introduces a deep learning-based approach to detecting and thwarting prompt injection attacks in LLM agent systems. Uses a hybrid model of known and customer-generated adversarial prompts to combine transformer-based classification, semantic risk-scoring and adaptive mitigation procedures. Stratified data splits are used in the experiments, as are synthetic attack generation and rule-based, BERT and zero-shot LLM classifiers. In terms of precision, recall, F1 score and AUC, the proposed framework is found to be better than all the baselines. Attack of instruction override, data extraction and tool misuse are greatly enhanced and resistant to adversarial scenarios that are not seen and adaptable. The mitigation module achieves high task utility; low false positive rates and the high success rate of the attacks is significantly reduced. Overall, the framework demonstrates that it is possible to integrate detection, risk estimation, and mitigation in a single pipeline, resulting in a great improvement in the security of LLM agents, while not burdening them with significant computing costs. It further highlights the importance of security layers before deploying LLM agents to the real world as the input they receive can be adversarial and continuously change, requiring a mixture of machine learning and structured control to ensure they remain safe and reliable across different application areas. Scalable AI systems deployment safety improvements involve multi-agent security, real-time learning, and multimodal prompt injection detection in the future.

radar.title: JaxMARL-BC: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Macroeconomic Modelling, in Seconds
radar.summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) offers a principled way of populating simulated economies with many heterogeneous decision makers. Its adoption, pioneered in finance, has nonetheless been slow in macroeconomics because of two main limitations: the lack of a shared frame of reference connecting MARL systems to dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models the profession already trusts, and the very long training times. The first limitation was recently addressed by the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Business Cycle (MARL-BC), which places deep RL households in a real business cycle economy and reduces to classic DSGE models in specific limits. Here we address the second limitation. We present JaxMARL-BC, a JAX-accelerated simulator that trains MARL-BC economies in seconds (between 75x and 724x faster than the reference implementation), and scales to 200,000 independent learning households. We verify its correctness against the known DSGE limits, characterise its scaling through a simple cost law, and demonstrate its value by a proof-of-concept calibration of an extended model with heterogeneous returns on capital, in a two-hour experiment that would previously have taken over a month. We release JaxMARL-BC as open source.

radar.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books
radar.summary: A market maker provides liquidity by quoting prices to buy and sell an asset, earning the spread while managing inventory risk. We study market makers trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning on prediction markets, specifically Polymarket, whose thin order books pose distinct challenges. Three challenges underpin this research: adverse selection may cause a policy trained on real data to stop quoting; the consequences of a quote can arrive many steps after the action; and prediction-market L2 data does not identify individual orders needed for simulation. We address these challenges by reconstructing order-level LOBSTER-format data from Polymarket and training agents in JaxMARL-HFT on 417 real markets. We enrich the baseline market maker's observation space with the book and recent flow, redesign its actions and inventory controls, and propose a cooperative multi-agent decomposition into a quoter and a risk manager trained using recurrent Independent Proximal Policy Optimisation (IPPO) with RNN policies. We investigate reward shaping, particularly reward blending and post-fill markout, to mitigate credit-assignment difficulties between the agents. Our redesigned single-agent market maker quotes more frequently and incurs smaller held-out losses than the retrained JaxMARL-HFT baseline, although the contributions of jointly changed observations, actions and risk constraints are not separately identified. Decomposition alone performs poorly; careful reward design substantially improves the desk relative to the unshaped split and yields our best result. Models are evaluated on realised end-of-episode portfolio value on held-out markets. None establishes positive average portfolio value in periodic held-out evaluation, and each configuration was trained with one seed. The environment, data and protocol lay a foundation for makers that quote many linked markets at once.

We study market makers trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning on prediction markets, specifically Polymarket, whose thin order books pose distinct challenges.

radar.title: Context-Aware Cooperative Gating for Knowledge-Controlled Value Factorization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

radar.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability requires decentralized agents to act from incomplete local information. Value-decomposition methods such as VDN and QMIX do not control when teammate-related knowledge may influence an agent’s local utility, and an uncontrolled teammate-conditioned term can distort decisions at timesteps where no ally is observable. We propose CA-QMIX, a context-aware value factorization method that uses ally visibility as a knowledge signal for decentralized agent control. Each agent combines an individual decision branch with an attention-based cooperative knowledge branch through a visibility-conditioned gate that scales the cooperative contribution and is hard-masked to zero when no ally is observable. The gated utilities are combined by a QMIX-style monotonic mixer, which we prove preserves Individual-Global-Max consistency, and a mixer-level Δ-Q regularizer discourages cooperative corrections that lower the greedy value of the base branch. Experiments on seven SMAC v1 and SMAC v2 scenarios against six value-decomposition baselines show that CA-QMIX attains the highest mean final win rate and the best mean rank over the seven scenarios and improves on QMIX in all three randomized SMAC v2 scenarios. Ablations show that most of the gain comes from the cooperative branch, that its visibility conditioning helps when correctly aligned (misaligned visibility degrades performance under randomized placement), and that the form of the gate is not critical: a binary gate suffices and the hard no-ally mask has no measurable cost.

In Which Matching Markets Do Costly Compatibility Inspections Lead to a Deadlock?
radar.summary: When Learning About a Match Stalls the Market In many matching markets, participants must investigate whether a match is feasible. When inspection is costly, participants may delay investigating a potential match until both sides have effectively committed. Such caution can cause each side to wait for others to act, creating an “information deadlock.” In their article, “In Which Matching Markets Do Costly Compatibility Inspections Lead to a Deadlock?” Immorlica, Kanoria, and Lu study this problem in random two-sided markets. They characterize how deadlock depends on the market balance, market connectivity, and the chance that inspections succeed. Using statistical physics tools, their analysis identifies phase transitions between deadlock-free and deadlocked markets. The findings offer design guidance: More choice is not always better; match rates are highest at the deadlock phase boundary; and parallel inspections and clearer participant differentiation can reduce the extent to which waiting chains stall the market.

radar.title: Trading Off Business and Family Investments: Evidence from U.S. Entrepreneurial Households
radar.summary: Investing in children’s human capital reduces business investments for U.S. entrepreneurial households. Using financial account data of 90,000 small businesses linked to their owners and a regression discontinuity design that compares the business performance of households with college-aged dependents (18–22) to those with near-college-aged dependents (14–17), I show that business revenues and expenses decline sharply when owners’ children reach age 18. Despite the declines, profitability and productivity remain largely unaffected, suggesting a general downsizing rather than a loss in efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows that downsizing is concentrated among highly indebted owner households and businesses with volatile cash flows. For each dollar increase in household spending associated with a child turning 18, business expenses decline by $2.26. These findings are consistent with entrepreneurial parents reallocating capital from business investments toward their children’s human capital, as both compete for the same pool of internal family financial resources. This paper was accepted by Camelia Kuhnen, finance. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04789 .

radar.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent
radar.summary: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni’s action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. Systematic benchmarking shows strong generalization across heterogeneous tasks—causal gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare-disease diagnosis, microbiome analysis, and molecular cloning—without task-specific tuning. Real-world case studies demonstrate Biomni interpreting multimodal datasets, optimizing protein stability, orchestrating wet-lab instruments, and generating experimentally testable protocols. Biomni envisions artificial intelligence augmenting human scientists and accelerating discovery.

radar.title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
radar.summary: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. A war forced into training is learned, but mostly only where it was forced. Against their own copies, deterred and matching agents can earn the same cartel profits, but only matching ones can enforce them, and then thinly: as a by-product and only against large cuts. Q-learners enforce collusion only in pricing. Prompted LLMs reach cartel-like outcomes mostly through rules that ignore the market. Outcome measures cannot tell these cases apart; the audit can.

radar.title: Constant Regret Primal-Dual Policy for Multiway Dynamic Matching
radar.summary: We study a discrete-time dynamic multiway matching model. There are finitely many agent types that arrive stochastically and wait to be matched. State-of-the-art dynamic matching policies in the literature require the knowledge of all system parameters to determine an optimal basis of the fluid relaxation, and focus on controlling the number of waiting agents using only matches within the optimal basis. In this paper, we propose a primal-dual policy that schedules matches for future arrivals based on an estimator for the dual solution. Our policy does not require the knowledge of the arrival rates and operates with greater flexibility as it does not restrict matches to only the match types within an optimal basis. We show that our policy is the first to achieve constant regret at all times under unknown arrival rates, and when the arrival rates are known, it achieves the optimal scaling. Furthermore, when the arrival rates are known, the primal-dual policy significantly outperforms alternative dynamic matching policies in several numerical simulations. radar.title: Vulnerability Analysis for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement
radar.summary: Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (SMARL) aims to learn cooperative control policies under prescribed safety constraints. Al- though existing SMARL methods focus on enforcing safety during policy optimization, their vulnerability remains largely unexplored. This paper investigates inference-time observation attacks against SMARL, where an adversary perturbs the observations of a subset of agents, thereby altering the actions produced by their policies. We propose MinMax Attack, an attack framework that jointly selects adversarial target actions for compromised agents while accounting for the Cooperative Resistance of benign agents. We further derive a bound on the induced safety cost and characterize its relation- ship with the Compromised-Agent Budget and the Perturbation Budget. Experiments across multiple safety-critical multi-agent benchmarks and representative state-of-the-art SMARL algorithms show that MinMax Attack induces substantially higher safety costs than existing attack baselines while preserving task reward, thereby reducing its detectability and achieving both attack effectiveness and stealthiness.

radar.title: Dynamic Contract Design with Learning
radar.summary: Incentivizing Effort While Learning the Market Condition When a firm hires an agent to generate customers in a new market, neither party initially knows whether the market is favorable. In “Dynamic Contract Design with Learning,” Wang, Liang, and Sun study the interaction between learning and moral hazard: effort is costly and unobservable, so a missing arrival may reflect an unfavorable market, bad luck, or shirking. The firm’s goal is to design a dynamic contract governing arrival-based payments and termination, thereby motivating effort while learning whether to continue. Yet shirking can make the principal more pessimistic than the agent and create scope to manipulate future payments. The authors prove that an optimal contract inducing full effort until termination exists, but computing it appears prohibitively complex. They develop two simple online contracts with payments and termination thresholds fixed in advance. Both induce full effort and achieve O(ln T) regret over T periods against a first-best, full-information benchmark. A matching Ω(ln T) lower bound proves rate optimality. The results extend to continuous time and differing prior beliefs.

radar.title: Who Directs the Control Tower? Customer vs. Supplier-Managed Inventory in Supply Chains
radar.summary: Information distortion and incentive misalignment often undermine supply chain performance. In response, many firms adopt a “control tower” approach, whereby one party assumes responsibility for replenishment decisions across the supply chain. Industry examples showed that this role may be assigned to the customer, Customer-Managed Inventory (CMI), or to the supplier, Supplier-Managed Inventory (SMI). This paper investigates when one governance structure is preferable. We study a two-echelon, one-to-many supply chain consisting of a single supplier and a customer operating multiple warehouses. We characterize optimal base-stock policies and equilibrium holding-cost-sharing parameters under CMI and SMI and benchmark them against decentralized operations and a fully centralized system. Two primary forces shape the choice between CMI and SMI: the relative shortage penalty costs of the two parties and the structure of the customer’s distribution network. Specifically, CMI is preferred when the customer faces relatively higher shortage penalties and operates in a more asymmetric environment—for example, when demand is concentrated in a subset of its warehouses or when replenishment lead times vary substantially across these locations. In contrast, SMI is favored under opposite conditions. We further examine how intertemporal and interspatial demand correlations affect this comparison. A key finding is that, although neither CMI nor SMI achieves the first-best outcome, their efficiency loss relative to full centralization is typically small. Calibrated numerical studies based on four industry cases disentangle the incremental value of information sharing, decision-right transfer, and cost sharing, showing that most performance gains stem from decision-right transfer supported by appropriate holding-cost sharing. This paper was accepted by Jayashankar Swaminathan, operations management. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02137 .

radar.title: Globally guided multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled critics for cooperative UAV path planning
radar.summary: Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Globally Guided Decoupled-Critic Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic algorithm (GDC-MASAC). RRT $$^*$$ -based global guidance provides reference waypoints for the leader UAV, reducing inefficient exploration and local deadlocks. Three decoupled Critic branches separately evaluate target navigation, formation maintenance, and safety objectives, while an environment-aware formation reward adjustment relaxes formation tracking near obstacles according to the distance to obstacle boundaries. Experiments under different obstacle densities and swarm sizes show that GDC-MASAC improves mission completion, collision avoidance, and formation coordination. In a scenario with 12 obstacles and 3 UAVs, GDC-MASAC achieves a mission success rate of 86%, whereas the baseline methods achieve success rates below 50%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GDC-MASAC for cooperative multi-UAV path planning in cluttered environments.

radar.title: EcoTrust-Net: A Causal, Explainable, and Energy-Aware Graph Transformer and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intelligent Network Traffic Prediction and Optimization
radar.summary: The increasing complexity of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems, Software-Defined Networking (SDN), edge intelligence, cloud-native infrastructures, and Internet of Things (IoT) environments has intensified the need for intelligent network traffic prediction and optimization capable of supporting low latency, high throughput, cyber-resilience, explainability, and energy-efficient operation. Existing approaches often address traffic prediction, routing optimization, explainability, or energy efficiency independently, resulting in limited topology awareness, weak causal interpretation, and reduced adaptability in highly dynamic communication environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes EcoTrust-Net, a causal, explainable, and energy-aware framework that integrates Graph Transformer-based topologyaware traffic prediction, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for adaptive routing and congestion control, Structural Causal Modeling (SCM) for causal inference and counterfactual reasoning, SHAP- and attention-based explainability, and multi-objective energy-aware optimization within a unified architecture. The framework was evaluated using heterogeneous datasets and environments comprising CAIDA backbone traffic traces, CIC-DDoS2019 attack traffic, Alibaba Cluster Trace workload data and NS-3/Mininet SDN simulations. Comparative experiments against conventional methods and recent state-of-the-art models published between 2024 and 2026, together with component-level ablation analysis, were conducted to assess prediction accuracy, Quality of Service (QoS), explainability, cyber-resilience and energy efficiency. Under the experimental conditions evaluated, EcoTrust-Net achieved 97.4% prediction accuracy, 96.8% precision, 96.1% recall, 96.4% F1-score, and an RMSE of 2.1. The framework also achieved 781 Mbps throughput, 12.4 ms latency, 1.8% packet loss, 97.1% attack detection, a 2.3% false-positive rate and 187 W energy consumption, outperforming the selected baseline models. These findings suggest that integrating topology-aware graph learning, cooperative reinforcement learning, causal reasoning, explainable artificial intelligence, and energy-aware optimization provides a promising framework for scalable, interpretable, and sustainable intelligent network traffic prediction and optimization in next-generation AI native communication networks.

radar.title: Graphexon Mean Field Games on Large Network Limits
radar.summary: This paper analyzes graphexon mean field games (GXMFG) on large network limits. By considering edge distributions of a sequence of finite graphs, we define the empirical graphexon measures and study their subsequential weak limits in a graphexon space consisting of all symmetric probability measures on $[0,1]^{2d}$. This concept of network limits extends graphon theory to general, not necessarily dense, networks. To formulate the game using the graphexon limit, we exploit a useful property that a probability measure on a product space is the product of a probability kernel and a marginal distribution. Based on such graph limits and the probability kernel of the associated graphexon measure, we derive the GXMFG equations, and present a detailed analysis for the linear-quadratic case. For linear-quadratic models with finite populations residing over large networks, we use the GXMFG equations to construct decentralized strategies, for which an $ε$-Nash equilibrium property is established.

radar.title: M-Plan: Comprehensive Planning For LLM Agents with Memory Arrangement
radar.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have recently demonstrated outstanding performance in single-turn tasks, yet they continue to struggle with long-horizon tasks, particularly in environments without prior training. A key limitation of single LLMs is their difficulty in processing long contexts, which stems from weaknesses in continuous decision-making and reasoning capabilities. Although existing multi-agent systems (MAS) equipped with long-term memory bases can partially address this gap, they mostly rely on knowledge reuse or summarization, an approach that is often constrained by directly retrieval without any adaptation for the current task, while the retrieved memory may contain much history noises waiting to be preprocessed. In contrast, MAS characterized by task-specific guidance often lack long-term memory specifically designed for the guidance. To address these challenges, we propose M-Plan, a closed-loop MAS framework that integrates long-term and short-term memory. By combining global-local and past-current guidance, M-Plan enhances agents' performance on multi-turn tasks while maintaining a plug-and-play design. During task execution, agents receive task-specific milestones and insights, and are provided with local hints only when confusion arises, which form global-local guidance together. These guidance generation and utilization construct the short-term memory as well. After task completion, relevant information about the current task is optimized or reorganized before being sent to the long-term memory storage for future retrieval. The designments mentioned above build a comprehensive framework different from other individual long-term or short-term memory works. Extensive experiments on multi-turn tasks including ALFWorld, Webshop, and PDDL across diverse models demonstrate that M-Plan outperforms multiple baseline methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

radar.title: Supply Chain Resilience Optimization Integrating Transformers and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.venue: ICST Transactions on Scalable Information Systems
radar.venue_raw: ICST Transactions on Scalable Information Systems
radar.summary: INTRODUCTION: Manufacturing supply chains face increasing vulnerabilities from delayed risk identification, conflicting node-level decisions, and escalating recovery costs, particularly under complex disruption scenarios. Existing approaches often lack proactive, coordinated responses across autonomous supply chain nodes, limiting their ability to anticipate disruptions and synchronize mitigation actions effectively. To address these gaps, this paper proposes an integrated resilience optimization framework that combines predictive analytics with multi-agent coordination. OBJECTIVES: The primary objective is to develop a supply chain resilience framework, termed T-MARL, that enables autonomous suppliers, manufacturers, warehousing nodes, and distributors to: (1) predict future disruption probabilities using temporal risk precursor data, and (2) execute coordinated, proactive replenishment, production, and distribution decisions under inventory and capacity constraints. The framework aims to improve resilience index, reduce total operating costs, and shorten recovery time compared to baseline strategies, while also examining the sensitivity of performance gains to prediction noise and communication latency. METHODS: The T-MARL framework models each supply chain node as an independent agent. A lightweight Transformer captures temporal features from 6-dimensional risk precursor sequences over 12 consecutive periods to forecast disruption probabilities. These predictions feed into a value-decomposition multi-agent reinforcement learning mechanism with centralized training–decentralized execution, where a value-decomposition network orchestrates cross-node actions. Risk-constrained action gating ensures that proactive responses adhere to inventory and capacity limits. A digital twin simulation environment was built with fixed random seeds, covering three scenarios—single-source supply disruption, demand surge, and compound disruption. Five strategies were tested, with 30 runs per unit using common random number pairing. RESULTS: On the trajectory-held-out test set, the Transformer achieved an AUC of 0.722 and an F1-score of 0.586, while Random Forest achieved a slightly higher AUC of 0.724. Under the compound disruption scenario, T-MARL attained a resilience index of 0.849—a 1.63 percentage-point gain over VDN-MARL -reduced total cost by 14.7%, and shortened average recovery time from 1.67 periods to zero. T-MARL also achieved lower operating costs while maintaining service levels comparable to rule-based strategies. However, the paper also found that prediction noise and communication latency diminish these performance gains. CONCLUSION: This research contributes a reproducible digital twin analysis framework for disruption prediction, cross-node collaborative response, and rapid recovery in manufacturing supply chains. While T-MARL demonstrates significant improvements in resilience and cost-efficiency under ideal conditions, practical deployment must account for real-world imperfections such as noisy forecasts and delayed communications. The framework provides a scalable foundation for future work on adaptive, data-driven supply chain resilience.

radar.title: Large language model multiagent systems for industrial problem discovery and prioritization
radar.summary: Abstract A persistent gap separates academic research priorities from the operational challenges faced by manufacturing firms. Established identification methods, among them Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) workshops, Lean audits and consultant engagements, are episodic, bounded by participant expertise and organised along departmental lines, which makes cross-departmental issues hard to surface. Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) have meanwhile shown collaborative problem-solving ability in software engineering and, more recently, in shopfloor scheduling and supply chain coordination. This article is a Perspective. It develops a framework and a research agenda; implementation and empirical evaluation fall outside its scope and are set out as its first research priorities. Three contributions are offered. The first is a synthesis of literature from industrial problem identification, LLM-based autonomous agents and manufacturing AI, which positions the proposal against existing industrial LLM agent work. The second is a framework in which six domain-specialised agents (production, quality, maintenance, supply chain, safety, energy) would collaborate through a five-phase protocol: worker-driven discovery, cross-departmental analysis, candidate-relationship detection, consensus-based financial assessment and debate-driven prioritisation. The prioritisation procedure is fully specified, including the normalisation of financial estimates, a measure of estimate dispersion, the derivation of criteria weights, a non-compensatory gate for safety-critical items and a mandatory human verification step. The third is a worked calculation on a hypothetical steel manufacturing vignette, included so that the procedure can be reproduced and scrutinised rather than as evidence of effectiveness. A preliminary qualitative readiness assessment and a three-horizon agenda of fourteen research questions complete the paper. The benefits identified are presented as hypotheses for that agenda to test rather than as demonstrated outcomes.

radar.title: Evolutionary-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning for waste electrical and electronic equipment inventory optimization under uncertainty
radar.summary: Waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) inventory optimization has attracted increasing attention with the growing emphasis on circular economy and sustainable development concepts. Effective uncertainty management is crucial for inventory optimization because recycling quantities fluctuate and custom order demands can arise unexpectedly. Although single-agent reinforcement learning methods can learn control policies for sequential decision-making tasks, they neglect collaboration and information sharing among multiple entities, making the resulting solutions unreliable in practical applications. In this paper, an evolutionary-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning (EAMARL) method is proposed to achieve multi-period, multi-echelon WEEE supply chain inventory optimization. Specifically, a control model is proposed for WEEE inventory optimization under uncertain recycling quantities and custom order demands. The model integrates make-to-order (MTO) and make-to-stock (MTS) production modes, and the resulting optimization problem is formulated as a decentralized Markov decision process. A multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm interacts with the WEEE supply chain environment to train control policies that maximize total profit. To address unstable convergence and limited exploration in MARL approaches, EAMARL integrates a population-based evolutionary algorithm that provides diverse exploratory experiences to support the training of MARL agents. Experiments in open-loop and closed-loop WEEE supply chain networks show that EAMARL improves average profit over the best-performing baseline by 12.09% and 14.39%, respectively. The normalized area under the learning curve of EAMARL indicates high learning efficiency and favorable convergence performance, while boxplot analysis demonstrates greater performance stability. Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and paired 95% confidence intervals further provide statistical support for the performance improvements.

radar.title: Sustainable Smart Grid Resilience and Renewable Integration Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: Sustainable energy systems must accommodate renewable generation to ensure dependable service during severe disruptions. This paper presents a decentralized multi-agent system that integrates feeder reconfiguration, Q-learning-based restoration, coordinated battery dispatch, and communication-efficient training. AC power flow validates restoration and voltage-control decisions on the IEEE 33-bus feeder and the synthetic 179-bus Oberrhein benchmark network. For single faults, decentralized restoration achieves the same result as exhaustive centralized search. For double faults across all 496 possible line-fault pairs, it restores 55.1% of isolated load, against 56.6% for centralized search, with 72.7% fewer feasibility evaluations. The learned single-switch policy reaches 95.2% of the oracle reward within its six-action set. Workload balancing reduces the time to target performance by a factor of 1.46. In a localized islanding case, coordinated storage raises fully served critical-load hours from 0% to 4.2%. Autonomous local Volt–VAr droop control increases photovoltaic (PV) hosting capacity by 51% over unity power factor without active power curtailment. Restoration performance degrades gradually under communication loss. An illustrative calculation gives 158–945 kg of avoided CO2 per storm event. All results come from simulation on benchmark networks.

radar.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
radar.summary: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.

radar.title: Near-Optimal Mechanisms for Resource Allocation Without Monetary Transfers
radar.summary: Aligning Incentives Without Opening the Wallet Many organizations must repeatedly allocate scarce resources—computing capacity, scientific equipment, school seats, or food-bank supplies—when monetary payments are impractical or undesirable. Blanchard and Jaillet show how future allocations can serve as rewards and penalties, inducing strategic agents to report their values truthfully while keeping welfare close to the full-information ideal. Their mechanisms use the promised utility framework and apply to general utility distributions in both finite-horizon and discounted infinite-horizon settings. The key insight is geometric; performance depends on the shape of the attainable-utility frontier. When agents often have similar values for the resource, the planner can shift allocations at little welfare cost and align incentives more effectively. The paper establishes universal convergence guarantees, faster rates for smooth utility distributions, and even exponentially small welfare losses in some discounted settings with frequent ties. The results provide a unified, quantitative framework for deciding when nonmonetary allocation can nearly match mechanisms that use payments.

radar.title: Autonomous AI-Driven Security Operations Centers (Autonomous SOC): Agentic Orchestration, Real-Time Incident Response, and Multi-Agent Defensive Playbooks
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: Abstract—Contemporary enterprise Security Operations Centers (SOCs) are on the brink of systemic collapse driven by three converging factors: exponential alert fatigue (>25,000 uninvestigated alerts daily per enterprise), acute global cybersecurity workforce shortages, and the emergence of automated, machine-speed cyber threats executing multi-stage Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) in sub-minute time horizons. Traditional Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platforms rely on brittle, rigid, hard-coded linear playbooks that fail when adversaries deviate slightly from known MITRE ATT&CK patterns. The paradigm of the Autonomous AI-Driven SOC (Autonomous SOC) establishes a transformative architecture that replaces rigid rule engines with specialized collaborative Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) powered by fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). In an Autonomous SOC, decentralized cognitive agents autonomously triage alerts, execute deep forensic graph correlation, synthesize non-linear incident playbooks, isolate compromised endpoints via zero-trust API invocations, and conduct automated counter-adversarial negotiations. However, deploying autonomous agentic execution in mission-critical defensive infrastructure exposes severe risks: catastrophic hallucination loops during remediation, prompt injection propagation across defensive pipelines, decision deadlock, and unauthorized disruption of legitimate enterprise operations. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Autonomous SOC architectures. We formalize incident response as a decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) under dynamic threat uncertainty, model consensus verification over cryptographic remediation DAGs, and establish a dual-tier human-on-the-loop (HOTL) safety gating mechanism. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise SOC evaluation testbed spanning 10,000 multi-stage attack scenarios across real-world enterprise topologies. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our multi-agent autonomous framework slashes Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) from 18.4 minutes to 4.2 seconds and Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) from 42.6 minutes to 18.2 seconds (a 99.3% reduction) while preserving a 99.6% remediation accuracy against MITRE ATT&CK kill chains. Finally, we formulate open challenges in adversarial prompt-injection resilience, continuous defensive co-evolution, and liability attribution under international cyber law. Index Terms—Autonomous SOC, Security Operations Center, Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), SOAR, Incident Response, MITRE ATT&CK, Dec-POMDP, Defensive AI, Alert Fatigue, Cyber Threat Intelligence.

radar.title: GSP Autobidding Equilibria with Few Advertisers or Slots
radar.summary: In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ranking. We prove that exact autobidding equilibria under budget and return-on-investment (ROI) constraints can be computed in polynomial time whenever either the number $n$ of advertisers or the number $K$ of display slots is fixed. Our algorithms rely on two structural reductions. With few advertisers, the payment polytopes of tied bid layers combine by a Minkowski sum, giving a fixed-dimensional representation of exponentially many rankings. With few slots, budget equilibria admit threshold recovery and an exact submodular description of attainable payments at the display boundary. For ROI, we prove that every group-consecutive equilibrium has a representative with at most $K+2$ nonunit multipliers, preserving the item and price in every displayed slot. In each case, the reduction leads to polynomially many systems of polynomial equations and inequalities in bounded dimension. The algorithms compute exact multipliers and explicit distributions over valid group-consecutive rankings, with support at most $n+1$; for ROI with few slots, this improves to $\min\{n+1,K+3\}$.

radar.title: Discrete Single-Parameter Optimal Auction Design
radar.venue_raw: ACM Transactions on Economics and Computation
radar.summary: We study the classic single-item auction setting of Myerson, but under the assumption that the buyers’ values for the item are distributed over finite supports. Using strong LP duality and polyhedral theory, we rederive various key results regarding the revenue-maximizing auction, including the characterization through virtual welfare maximization and the optimality of deterministic mechanisms, as well as a novel, generic equivalence between dominant-strategy and Bayesian incentive compatibility. Inspired by this, we abstract our approach to handle more general auction settings, where the feasibility space can be given by arbitrary convex constraints, and the objective is a linear combination of revenue and social welfare. We characterize the optimal auctions of such systems as generalized virtual welfare maximizers, by making use of their KKT conditions, and we present an analogue of Myerson’s payment formula for general discrete single-parameter auction settings. Additionally, we prove that integrality of the feasibility space is a sufficient condition to guarantee the optimality of auctions with integral allocation rules. Finally, we demonstrate this KKT approach by applying it to a setting where bidders are interested in buying feasible flows on trees with capacity constraints, and provide a combinatorial description of the (randomized, in general) optimal auction.

Are language models rational? The case of coherence norms and belief revision
radar.summary: Do norms of rationality apply to machine learning models, in particular language models? In this paper we investigate this question by focusing on a special subset of rational norms: coherence norms. We consider both logical coherence norms as well as coherence norms tied to the strength of belief. To make sense of the latter, we introduce the Minimal Assent Connection (MAC) and propose a new account of credence, which captures the strength of belief in language models. This proposal uniformly assigns strength of belief simply on the basis of model-internal next token probabilities. We argue that rational norms tied to coherence do apply to some language models but not to others. This issue is significant since rationality is closely tied to predicting and explaining behavior, and thus it is connected to considerations about AI safety and alignment, as well as understanding model behavior more generally.
